claim: `module.exports` is used in a file Node loads as an ES module, so `module` is unbound and the whole file throws at load time.
impact: The first consumer of demo/cart.js gets `ReferenceError: module is not defined in ES module scope` before any export resolves, so `subtotal`, `applyDiscount` and `logOrder` become unreachable too.
why: There is no package.json anywhere in the tree, so Node's module-syntax detection classifies this file as ESM from the pre-existing `export function` declarations on lines 1, 5 and 10. The skeptic reproduced the failure on the repo's Node v26.7.0 across every load path — `node demo/cart.js`, static `import`, dynamic `import()`, and `require()` — all failing identically at line 25. The damage is not limited to the new helper: the three pre-existing exports are lost with it, and `unsafeEval` is never actually exported by any path (the resolved namespace is `['subtotal','applyDiscount','logOrder']`). Adding `"type":"commonjs"` does not help; it converts lines 1/5/10 into a SyntaxError instead. Held at concern rather than must-fix because nothing in the repo imports demo/cart.js today — it is a synthetic fixture that setup-demo.sh:162 overwrites from demo/.seed/cart.js — so no test goes red right now; it breaks the first change that consumes the file. No one-click fix is offered deliberately: the mechanical repair (`export function unsafeEval`) would make `eval(expr)` on a caller-supplied string a genuinely exported sink, which is strictly worse than the current broken state where it is unreachable. The right fix is to delete the added block (lines 21-25) entirely, which removes both the load-time crash and the eval, and a deletion is not expressible as a replacement suggestion.
